audit.scope: agents (15), skills (51), memory (1), settings (1); user-global tree inventoried for precedence only

dissolved_on_verification.claim: No agent declares the Skill tool, so 'Load the <skill> skill' directives are unsatisfiable
dissolved_on_verification.resolution: Not a finding. The Skill tool is available to subagents regardless of the tools: allowlist per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md. All 8 load directives work as written.

dissolved_on_verification.claim: TaskCreate may not be a valid frontmatter tool name
dissolved_on_verification.resolution: Not a finding. TaskCreate is documented and valid. The 7 agents declaring it are correct.

superseded.verdict: The 2026-08-04 resolution above was wrong. It is kept verbatim, not deleted, because the precedent it set is the point: an authoritative one-line dissolution stopped anyone opening an agent body for a month.
why_it_was_wrong: It answered a question nobody needed answered. The claim was about name validity; the registry invariant at .claude/README.md:200 is that every tool in tools: must be exercised by a procedure in the body. Validity is necessary, not sufficient, and the resolution never opened a body to check the sufficient half.

No agent body in any tree contains a procedure that uses the grant. That was true on 2026-08-04 and is the entire finding. It holds regardless of whether the name resolves, which is why it is the justification for dropping the grant.

'documented and valid' cited no document. TaskCreate is absent from the current Claude Code tool registry, which exposes TaskOutput and TaskStop; no tree references either of those. That is a second and independent reason the grants were inert, but it is not the reason they were dropped.
superseded.the_grant_set_churned_rather_than_grew: 'The 7 agents declaring it are correct' reads as a stable, reviewed set. It was not. .claude/audit/AUDIT.md:92 names database-engineer and performance-engineer as declarers; neither declares it today (both now carry Agent(qa-runner) instead). The eight declarers measured on 2026-09-02 were incident-commander, product-analyst, product-manager, qa-engineer, release-manager, software-engineer, solution-architect, ui-engineer. The membership turned over while the 'correct' verdict was carried forward unexamined, which is worse precedent than a set that merely grew from 7 to 8: nobody re-derived the verdict for the members that were added.
superseded.action_taken: Grant dropped at 34 sites: 8 TaskCreate frontmatters in .claude/agents/, 8 in sdlc-suite/agents/, 8 task_create in commandcode-suite/agents/, 8 create-task in .copilot/agents/*.json, and the two converter map entries at commandcode-suite/convert-agents.py and .copilot/convert-agents.py. The map entries were load-bearing: measured before the change, a regeneration of all four harnesses reintroduced the grant into 16 generated definitions; measured after, 0.
superseded.a_tempting_but_backwards_argument_not_to: Do not argue that commandcode-suite granting TaskCreate to none of its agents shows the name is harness-specific. Two converters translated it (TaskCreate -> task_create, TaskCreate -> create-task), which is evidence it was treated as portable. That false negative came from grepping the literal string across trees whose converters rename it.
superseded.residual_references_left_deliberately: commandcode-suite/validate.py:27 keeps task_create in KNOWN_TOOLS. That list is Command Code's tool vocabulary, not a grant, and is correctly unaffected by whether any agent uses it. .claude/audit/AUDIT.md:92 still names the two former declarers; it is left intact because its staleness is the evidence this entry cites.
superseded.totals_unchanged: This supersedes a dissolved_on_verification entry, not a findings[] entry, so audit.totals is untouched and remains accurate.

findings.finding: No agent in the registry declares the Agent tool, so no agent can invoke qa-runner. Delegation to it is instructed in prose across four agents.
findings.evidence: agents/qa-engineer.md:4 tools list omits Agent; agents/database-engineer.md:4, agents/performance-engineer.md:4, agents/incident-commander.md:4 likewise. Delegation instructed at agents/qa-engineer.md sec 9.1, agents/qa-runner.md:3, agents/qa-runner.md:27, agents/incident-commander.md:3. Docs confirm Agent must be listed in tools: for a subagent to spawn subagents.
findings.impact: qa-runner's sole purpose is keeping large raw output out of a reasoning agent's context. It is unreachable, so that protection silently does not work and qa-engineer will flood its own context via Bash instead.
findings.recommendation: Add scoped Agent(qa-runner) to qa-engineer, database-engineer, performance-engineer. Decide explicitly what incident-commander may spawn, or reword its description to drop the coordination claim.

findings.finding: qa-engineer is the only agent that systematically calls domain skills. The other 14 inline their domain knowledge and name zero domain skills, leaving 36+ of 51 skills unreachable.
findings.evidence: Wired: qa-engineer.md:133,163,222,249; product-analyst.md:71; incident-commander.md:92; technical-writer.md:19. Unwired with inline duplication: ux-designer.md:58,64,70,73 duplicate skills/ux-research/SKILL.md:8, skills/interaction-design/SKILL.md:8, skills/accessibility/SKILL.md:10-19, skills/design-systems/SKILL.md:12 while naming none of them; solution-architect.md:75 duplicates skills/architecture-decisions/SKILL.md:12-20; code-reviewer.md names no code-review-craft; performance-engineer.md names neither performance-engineering nor capacity-planning; release-manager.md names none of release-engineering/rollback-strategies/feature-flagging; security-engineer.md names none of threat-modeling/secure-coding/supply-chain-security/privacy-engineering; site-reliability.md names none of observability-design/capacity-planning/disaster-recovery.
findings.impact: 36+ skills have no caller, so the better-written half of the registry rarely if ever fires while agents run a thinner duplicated copy inline; the two copies will drift. Scoping note: description-based auto-triggering INSIDE a subagent is undocumented rather than documented as absent, so the supportable claim is that an unnamed skill cannot be relied on to load. The finding does not depend on resolving this - 14 agents inlining a thinner duplicate of content the skill layer owns better is a defect either way.
findings.recommendation: Wire, do not delete. Add explicit 'Load the <skill> skill' directives at the point of use in each owning agent following the qa-engineer pattern, then thin the now-redundant inline prose. Shrinks agents and makes skills reachable in one move.

findings.finding: The memory root is specified two incompatible ways: canonical '.claude/memory/<project>/' and bare relative 'memory/<project>/'.
findings.evidence: Canonical: skills/project-memory/SKILL.md:8, agents/qa-engineer.md:298, agents/code-reviewer.md:151. Bare: agents/product-manager.md:93,109; agents/product-analyst.md:95,101,115; agents/incident-commander.md:146; agents/release-manager.md:107; agents/technical-writer.md:31; agents/ux-designer.md:115; skills/risk-management/SKILL.md:10; skills/stakeholder-management/SKILL.md:10; skills/technical-debt-management/SKILL.md:10; skills/retrospectives/SKILL.md:22; skills/disaster-recovery/SKILL.md:26; skills/ux-research/SKILL.md:26; skills/architecture-decisions/SKILL.md:25; skills/analytics-and-telemetry/SKILL.md:26; memory/README.md:8.
findings.impact: PROSPECTIVE, not yet observed: .claude/memory/ contains only README.md and no <repo>/memory/ exists, so nothing has been written to either location and no memory has been lost yet. But the relative form resolves against cwd, so once agents persist, writers will land in <repo>/memory/ while readers look in <repo>/.claude/memory/. Cross-agent memory handoff will silently fail, presenting as an empty/missing file, which memory/README.md:24 instructs agents to read as 'nothing recorded yet' - indistinguishable from valid information. Fixing before first use costs 20 lines; after, a data migration.
findings.recommendation: Mechanical replace to .claude/memory/<project>/ across all 18 files. Direction is a judgment call, stated explicitly: the bare form is the numerical majority (16 sites vs 3), but .claude/memory/<project>/ is treated as canonical because skills/project-memory/SKILL.md:3,8 is the artifact that defines the convention and the memory root genuinely lives inside .claude/.

findings.finding: No skill description carries negative scope. 51/51 state a positive trigger; none state a 'do NOT use for' clause.
findings.evidence: skills/api-design/SKILL.md:3, skills/system-architecture/SKILL.md:3, skills/accessibility/SKILL.md:3, skills/capacity-planning/SKILL.md:3 - all positive-trigger only.
findings.impact: Reduced by WIRE-01 (selection should be by explicit agent directive, not description match). Still material for the adjacent pairs a human or main-loop invoker must choose between.
findings.recommendation: Add negative scope only to the ~8 skills in genuinely adjacent pairs (capacity-planning/performance-engineering, disaster-recovery/business-continuity, api-versioning/backward-compatibility, documentation vs technical-writer). Do not edit all 51.

findings.finding: technical-writer.md is structurally out of family: 33 lines vs 62-305 for peers, with no numbered sections, no proportionality tiers, no evidence classification, no stop conditions, and no engineering-integrity/project-memory load directive.
findings.evidence: agents/technical-writer.md:3 omits the 'Loads the ... skills' clause peers carry (contrast agents/ux-designer.md:3); no equivalent of agents/ux-designer.md:11 load directive; agents/technical-writer.md:31 instructs memory persistence with no convention loaded; quality bar at :40 demands verification with no vocabulary to express an unverifiable claim.
findings.impact: The only agent producing durable, externally-consumed artifacts has the weakest verification discipline and no memory protocol.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite to family structure. Draft provided at audit/proposed/technical-writer.md.

findings.finding: No agent declares model:; all 15 inherit. Appropriate for 14, but qa-runner is an explicitly no-judgment mechanical executor.
findings.evidence: All agent frontmatter is name/description/tools only. agents/qa-runner.md:13 ('You do not decide what should be tested...'), :17 ('You deliberately have no tiering and no memory').
findings.impact: qa-runner inherits the main-conversation model for work that is mechanical by design.
findings.recommendation: Set an explicit lighter tier on qa-runner only; leave the other 14 inheriting and state that as deliberate.

findings.artifact: software-engineer, solution-architect, security-engineer, site-reliability, ux-designer, product-analyst
findings.finding: The skills: preload frontmatter field is unused, though six agents commit to loading two skills unconditionally.
findings.evidence: agents/ux-designer.md:3 and :11; agents/solution-architect.md:3 and :11; agents/security-engineer.md:3 and :11; agents/site-reliability.md:3 and :11; agents/software-engineer.md:3 and :11. No agent declares skills:.
findings.impact: Costs a tool round-trip per agent per session on two always-wanted skills, and makes the guarantee depend on the model obeying a prose line rather than being structural.
findings.recommendation: Add 'skills: [engineering-integrity, project-memory]' to the agents that load unconditionally; drop the redundant prose directive.

findings.finding: qa-runner holds Write with no documented need.
findings.evidence: agents/qa-runner.md:4 grants Write; :3 charters it as 'returns factual execution evidence - nothing interpreted'; :17 makes it explicitly memory-less. No procedure in the 62-line body writes a file.
findings.impact: Write capability on the one agent defined by having no judgment - the profile where least-privilege matters most.
findings.recommendation: Drop Write, or document the artifact it produces.

findings.finding: code-reviewer's description asserts it is read-only and 'does not execute', but its tools grant includes Bash.
findings.evidence: agents/code-reviewer.md:3 'Read-only; never modifies code... this agent reads and reasons, it does not execute' vs :4 'tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash'.
findings.impact: The description contradicts the grant and asserts non-execution to the orchestrator while execute capability is present. Almost certainly intentional for git diff/git log.
findings.recommendation: State the intended read-only Bash scope in the body, or remove Bash.

findings.finding: The documentation skill claims the technical-writer agent's entire remit; neither states the boundary.
findings.evidence: agents/technical-writer.md:19 loads documentation for 'structure conventions'; skills/documentation/SKILL.md:3 claims 'Structure and quality bar for technical documentation... Load when writing or updating any documentation artifact'.
findings.impact: Both are justified (DELINEATE, not merge), but an invoker cannot tell which owns what.
findings.recommendation: Scope the skill to conventions/mechanics and the agent to authorship/verification, explicitly on both sides.

findings.finding: dependency-management's Updating section restates dependency-upgrades nearly verbatim. The only genuine near-duplicate pair in the registry.
findings.evidence: skills/dependency-management/SKILL.md:16-18 ('Prefer frequent small updates over rare large ones... don't bump blindly because a bot opened a PR') vs skills/dependency-upgrades/SKILL.md:8-14 (same two claims). An orchestrator choosing between them for an upgrade task is a coin flip.
findings.impact: Duplicated guidance that will drift; ambiguous selection.
findings.recommendation: MERGE to a single dependency-health skill. Draft at audit/proposed/dependency-health/SKILL.md.

findings.finding: References playwright-best-practices and playwright-cli, which exist only in the user-global skills tree.
findings.evidence: skills/qa-tooling/SKILL.md:27 '(see playwright-best-practices / playwright-cli skills)'; neither exists under .claude/skills/. Both exist under %USERPROFILE%/.claude/skills/.
findings.impact: Resolves on this machine only; the project tree is otherwise fully self-contained.
findings.recommendation: Vendor them into the project tree, or mark the reference as environment-dependent.

findings.finding: A PreToolUse hook on Bash runs 'rtk hook claude', a user-local binary. Ten of 15 agents hold Bash and route through it.
findings.evidence: %USERPROFILE%/.claude/settings.json hooks.PreToolUse matcher 'Bash' command 'rtk hook claude'; rtk resolves to C:/Users/avega/.local/bin/rtk.exe.
findings.impact: On a machine without rtk, every Bash call in the suite hits a missing-binary hook. Outside the audited project tree, so advisory - and notably the project tree itself has no such coupling.
findings.recommendation: Guard the hook on binary presence, or document rtk as an environment prerequisite. Requires a separate decision - not in project scope.

findings.finding: disabledMcpjsonServers lists 'webmcp', but no .mcp.json exists anywhere under the repo.
findings.evidence: settings.local.json disabledMcpjsonServers: ["webmcp"]; recursive search for .mcp.json under the repo returns nothing.

findings.finding: software-engineer and the accessibility skill exist in both the project and user-global trees; project definitions win, leaving the user-global copies inert here.
findings.evidence: agents/software-engineer.md (179 lines) vs %USERPROFILE%/.claude/agents/software-engineer.md (241 lines); skills/accessibility/SKILL.md vs %USERPROFILE%/.claude/skills/accessibility/.
findings.impact: The risk is editing the wrong file in a later session - the user-global software-engineer is 62 lines longer, so it looks like the more developed one.
findings.recommendation: Delete or rename the user-global copies, or add a header note marking them superseded. Outside project scope - requires a separate decision.

remediation.process_note: The first PATH-01 pass used Get-Content -Raw + WriteAllText, which in PowerShell 5.1 read UTF-8 as cp1252 and double-encoded every em-dash and section sign in 16 files. Caught on the next read, reversed via cp1252 round-trip, verified 0 mojibake remaining. All later edits used the editor rather than shell rewrites. Future bulk edits of this tree must not round-trip through Get-Content -Raw.

verified_clean: No secrets, tokens, API keys, tenant IDs, org URLs, client/employer names, internal hostnames, or project keys anywhere in the project tree.
No absolute paths and no username-bearing paths in the project tree.
No shell-specific syntax in any artifact - no artifact contains a shell command at all, so cross-platform quoting and path-separator breakage cannot occur.
No '|| true', no swallowed exit codes, no procedure that continues past a failed step.

No --force/--yes/force-push instruction except inside explicit prohibitions at agents/software-engineer.md:192 and skills/engineering-integrity/SKILL.md:55; destructive-action gates are present and judge by blast radius and reversibility.
No recursive delegation cycle - though note this is currently vacuous: per DELEG-01 no delegation is possible at all, so re-check this property after DELEG-01 is fixed.
No stale pinned versions, deprecated flags, or aged-out 'current as of' claims.
All 15 agent and 51 skill frontmatter blocks parse cleanly; every name is kebab-case, unique, and matches its filename stem.
Agent descriptions are genuine routing signals with negative scope, not nominal labels.
No skill exceeds 36 lines, so progressive-disclosure bloat is not a concern.
Every inter-agent handoff target named across the 15 agents resolves to a real configured agent; the lifecycle is closed with no unowned stage.
No agent/skill category errors; no skill needs promoting to an agent and no agent demoting to a skill.
Portability: 15/15 agents and 51/51 skills score 'pass' against both a Rust/Cargo CLI and a COBOL/DB2 mainframe project. No artifact requires adapter changes.
No capability-abstraction layer is needed - skills/qa-tooling/SKILL.md:12-31 already implements detection-signal to implementation mapping correctly, enforced as policy at agents/qa-engineer.md:163.
